text:
Connor McMichael came to St. Louis in June in the Jordan Kyrou trade and signed a six-year deal a few weeks later, so the Blues are counting on him. The first month in a new city has been uneven: nine points in 19 games, two goals, and none in his last ten. The Hockey News noticed it too, grouping him with Mason McTavish as players who started hot and cooled.

Some of the slump is luck. St. Louis has scored 7.3 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice, the kind of gap that usually swings back, and he's shooting 7.4% against roughly 12% our numbers expect from him.

The part that isn't luck is defense. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.18 more expected goals per 60 with him on the ice last season, bottom 5% of forwards, and his team is roughly even in chance share now. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 60% of his shots coming off the rush. When the rush offense is quiet, the rest of his game has to carry more.
headline: McMichael has gone cold in St. Louis
